case.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Open Source Program Office (Open Source Program Group since June 2026)
case.local_name: CMS OSPO, Digital Service at CMS (DSACMS)
case.jurisdiction: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
case.status: operating (reorganized into the Open Source Program Group, Office of Health Technology and Products, June 2026)

authorizing_act.title: Statement of Organization, Functions, and Delegations of Authority (FR Doc. 2026-11743, 91 FR 35478). Before June 2026 the office ran on a functional statement, not a charter.
authorizing_act.body: CMS / U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Federal Register

case.placement: Inside the Digital Service at CMS (a U.S. Digital Service agency team) 2023-2026; from June 2026 one of four groups in the new Office of Health Technology and Products

headcount.note: About five per a 2025 Beeck Center profile (DeCausemaker, Kopelevich, Panayil, Luzuriaga, Milarsky). Headcount after the June 2026 reorganization unverified.

case.role_in_procurement_detail: The office wrote the agency's Inbound Review Checklist, which imports OMB M-16-21's three-step analysis and the agency's total-cost-of-ownership rules, but the sign-offs are a code reviewer, the security officer, the infrastructure group and the business owner; the OSPO is not among them. Licensing is approved by the Technical Review Board; legal review is General Counsel's; policy is led by the Technical Reference Architecture; contract clauses come from acquisitions. The June 2026 charter gives the parent office 'acquisition oversight, including preference for commercial off-the-shelf and common contract solutions.' Exemptions from release go to OMB and Congress; no public register.
functions: outbound code release: tiered checklists, release guidelines, maturity model
custom code inventory (code.json) and SHARE IT Act compliance tooling
risk acceptance and exemption criteria for code that stays closed (decided by security, infrastructure and business owners)
repository scaffolding, linting rules and metrics dashboard
guidance site (ospo-guide) including 'Want to Start an OSPO'
ensuring at least 20% of newly developed custom code is released as open source (June 2026 charter)

un_principles_mapping.open_by_default: 20% release floor (M-16-21; 2026 charter); exemption criteria exist but the decision belongs to security and business owners, with no public register
un_principles_mapping.contribute_back: integrates the CHAOSS project's Augur; outside contributions reported
un_principles_mapping.secure_by_design: security sign-off on every release; repolinter rulesets; 'libyears' dependency-age metric
un_principles_mapping.foster_inclusive_participation: talent pipelines; U.S. Digital Corps fellows on the team
un_principles_mapping.design_for_reusability: everything CC0 / public domain; repo-scaffolder, maturity model and checklists written to be copied
un_principles_mapping.provide_documentation: ospo-guide site with inbound, outbound and growing sections
un_principles_mapping.rise: 'Want to Start an OSPO' guidance; FedScoop recognition for the lead
un_principles_mapping.sustain_and_scale: metrics dashboard; office survived administration change and reorganization because its work was public, but had no charter for 2.5 years

lessons_for_nyc: Adopt the public-domain kit in month one: maturity model, tiered checklists, exemption criteria, metrics pipeline, code.json tooling.
Translate M-16-21's three-step analysis and 20% release rule and the SHARE IT Act's inventory and exemption reporting into a city rule.
Put the inbound review in the office's hands: required review of contracts above a threshold, ownership of the options analysis, a public exceptions register.
Create the office by Council legislation rather than functional statement so its mandate cannot be dissolved by memo.
Publish everything in the public domain; CMS's code outlived its office because it was public.
Report annually on contracts reviewed, exceptions granted and code released; CMS has published none of these counts.
